name: SpaceX
day_summary: Saturday — US equity markets closed. No SPCX trading. SPCX remains in STEP_ASIDE mode at the confirmed last close of $174.90 (June 18), $10.10 below the $185 daily-close stop. MAJOR WEEKEND DEVELOPMENT: SpaceX received investment-grade credit ratings from all three major agencies on June 18-19: Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, S&P Global BBB — all with stable outlook (Reuters/Yahoo Finance/IndexBox). This is a fundamental long-term positive for SPCX that has not yet been priced in (markets were closed June 19 Juneteenth and June 20 Saturday). Monday June 22 is the first opportunity to price in the investment-grade ratings. The ratings were issued less than a week after the record $85.7B IPO. Moody's specifically cited 'exceptional franchise strength' as the world's leading orbital launch provider; Fitch cited >80% global mass-to-orbit share since 2023. The Moody's Baa1 rating is notably higher than Tesla's Baa3. Additional context: June 20 weekly options expiry CLEARED (the $195 max-pain gamma headwind expired at Friday June 19 Juneteenth settlement prices); DXY declining to ~100.23 weekend (from 100.79 Thursday) is the most constructive macro development for the 84x revenue multiple. June 22 open remains the key diagnostic: the investment-grade ratings + DXY improving could catalyze a stronger opening than expected for a stock that was -18.3% from its Day 3 ATH.
long_pnl: IPO allocants from $135 are +29.6% at $174.90 — still in the money; any FOMC-dip buyer from $187–$192 (Days 4–5) has exited per the $185 stop; investment-grade ratings (S&P BBB, Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+) are a structural positive for the long-term thesis that lowers SPCX's cost of capital and expands the institutional buyer universe to include fixed-income-mandate investors; position is stepped aside, not broken
short_pnl: bears validated thesis from Day 4 peak ($213.80) to $174.90 (−18.3%); however, investment-grade ratings from S&P, Moody's, and Fitch arriving simultaneously is the most significant fundamental positive since the IPO — it validates the franchise quality at a structural level; DXY declining to 100.23 removes the primary 'multiple compression' macro support for the short; June 22 is the bear diagnostic: if SPCX gaps up significantly on IG rating news, a portion of the short thesis has been invalidated

decision.horizon: reassessment — June 22 open diagnostic; IG ratings as gap-up catalyst
decision.rationale: STEP ASIDE at HIGH conviction — framework unchanged but thesis improving materially. The $185 daily close stop triggered at $174.90 on June 18 — $10.10 below threshold. No re-entry before two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume. HOWEVER: Investment-grade credit ratings from S&P (BBB), Moody's (Baa1), and Fitch (BBB+) issued June 18-19 — unpriced for 3 days due to Juneteenth + Saturday closure — could drive a significant gap-up on June 22 open. If SPCX opens at or above $185 on June 22 driven by IG rating news, that changes the diagnostic framework. Scenarios: (1) SPCX opens $165–$175 with recovering volume (>150M shares) → stabilization watch, IG ratings positive; (2) SPCX opens $175–$185 on IG rating enthusiasm → begin 3–5 session watch, stop at $165; (3) SPCX opens at or above $185 on IG momentum → wait for a CLOSE above $185 plus one additional close (still need 2 consecutive closes); (4) Opens below $165 → correction extending, IG ratings insufficient to reverse near-term trend. July options at ~52–55% IV remain the preferred hedge vehicle. September 2 first earnings print is the fundamental anchor.

A July $175 put (downside protection for any re-entry near $185) would cost approximately $12–14 at current IV.

outlook.short_term: Investment-grade credit ratings transform the June 22 diagnostic. The three-day market closure (Juneteenth + Saturday) means the Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, and S&P BBB ratings have not yet been priced into the equity. If SPCX gaps toward $185+ on June 22 open driven by IG rating news, the step_aside framework approaches its re-engagement trigger from below. Scenarios: (1) IG ratings + DXY improving + clean options slate = gap toward $185 on June 22 open; watch for two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume; (2) Even if gap-up falls short of $185, the IG ratings fundamentally alter the July options hedge structure — lower cost of capital = lower fair-value IV = cheaper put protection for any new long position.
outlook.long_term: Generational franchise, now with investment-grade validation. The trifecta of Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, and S&P BBB — issued simultaneously within days of the IPO — confirms that the three most credentialed institutional risk assessors in the world have independently reviewed SpaceX's cash flows and found them investment-grade quality. This is the most important fundamental development for SPCX since the IPO: it opens the bond market at investment-grade rates, expands the institutional buyer universe to fixed-income mandates, and permanently reduces the franchise's cost of capital. Combined with Starlink growth, Starship launch economics, Starshield, and Cursor AI, the September 2 first earnings print becomes even more critical as the catalyst to unlock the full IG-grade valuation reset.
